newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended mixed on Monday, temporarily pausing in their recent rally.
After dipping during the morning in a continuing move of late Friday's profit-taking, prices recovered as only few parties were eager to sell their positions.

The 1998 benchmark ended unchanged, yielding 3.29 percent at bid, the new ten-year benchmark added two basis points to 102.82/92 for a bid yield of 5.38 percent, while the 2023 bond added 0.12 points to close at 118.35/55, yielding 6.07 percent.
Dealers said the long bond attracted much attention as professional players continued to try to switch into longer maturities, but added finally not many trades were done.
The new ten-year benchmark, in which trade was more liquid, was said to be comparatively active in the overall quiet market.

"There's not much special that can be said about today's trade in the ten-years, but a 5.38 percent yield on a ten-year state loan is very unusual, and so is the recent rise in this bond's price," one dealer said.
Dealers said the closure of the American market was among the reasons for the volume to be extremely thin in both state and corporate issues.

"After the rally of the last two weeks, with American markets closed and some important figures coming up, there is no leading idea in the market," one dealer said, adding this caused a wait and see attitude.
He said he expected Dutch bond prices to remain stable in slow trade on Tuesday morning as well until the U.S. opening might trigger activity.
